chunks: Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Daylamī narrated from his father, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who gives part of his house in charity to a stranger, then dies. He said: “That should be appraised at its value, then its price should be paid to him.”
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man donates part of his house to a stranger and then dies?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a charitable transfer of part of a house to a non-relative when the donor dies. The Imam عليه السلام states that the donated portion is to be assessed by value and its price paid, indicating a juristic treatment of the gift through monetary valuation.
